class.name: PhysXLensDirt3D
class.brief_description: Lens dirt lit by the frame's bright light, provided by the PhysX module.
class.description: Dust, smudges and droplet marks on the camera lens that light up where bright light reaches it: the frame's bright light, spread wide the way a lens scatters it, multiplies [member dirt_texture] and is added on top -- the way other engines' bloom dirt masks work. Any bright light does it (the sky, the sun, fire, headlights, [PhysXLightShafts3D]'s rays, [PhysXLensFlare3D]'s ghosts, [PhysXFlow3D] flames); where the texture is black, or nothing in that part of the screen is bright, the frame is untouched. Add the node anywhere in the scene and give it a texture. Not the same as [member Environment.glow_map], which [i]multiplies[/i] Godot's glow by a texture (dimming the glow where the texture is dark) rather than adding light where the texture has dirt. The texture is stretched over the screen: author it at the screen's aspect ratio (typically 16:9), with the dirt bright on black. The demo project's [code]demo/common/textures/lens_dirt.png[/code] is an example. Works with the Forward+ and Mobile renderers, not Compatibility (which has no compositor effects). Only one [PhysXLensDirt3D] is drawn per frame; with several, which one is unspecified.

members.member: The dirt on the lens: bright where there's dirt, black where the glass is clean. Stretched over the screen. Nothing is drawn without one.
How bright the lit dirt is.

How bright (linear HDR luminance) a part of the frame must be before it lights the dirt. At [code]0[/code] all light counts, more where it's brighter -- a dirty lens shows against a bright sky as well as around the sun. In Godot's default scenes the sky is around [code]0.5[/code] and only the sun's disk goes above [code]1[/code], so raising it toward [code]1[/code] keeps the dirt to the brightest sources.
